title: BACnet/IP
source: ASHRAE 135 (BACnet) Annex J — BACnet/IP, §6 network layer, §20 encoding

about: BACnet/IP — ASHRAE 135 Annex J, on UDP 47808. Three layers in one datagram: BVLC says how long
the whole thing is, NPDU says whether it is routed and how urgent, APDU says what is being asked.
Which of the four PDU types this is, is the top nibble of the seventh octet — so the reading looks
at six octets and a nibble before choosing, and each PDU type is then a single path from the first
octet to the last, exactly as though it were the only one here.
WHAT THIS DESCRIBES. ReadProperty and what comes back from it: the Confirmed-Request, the
ComplexACK (whole, and the first segment of a segmented one), the SegmentACK that paces segments,
and the Error that arrives instead. Every one of those limits is CHECKED rather than assumed — a
routed NPDU, a BVLC function that is not Original-Unicast, a service that is not ReadProperty are
each refused where they are written.
WHAT IT DOES NOT. A segment's payload is opaque, and that is not a shortfall: ASHRAE 135 §5.3 cuts
the service payload at whatever octet the window ran out on — capture C3 stops halfway through an
object identifier — so no segment is parseable on its own. The thing to parse is the
concatenation of the segments, which is a buffer that never appears on any wire, and assembling it
is the client's across several datagrams rather than this description's within one.

about: Annex J.2.1: the length of the WHOLE BVLL message, these four octets included.
A length that measures the span it sits in, which is not the cycle it looks like: this field
is two octets wide whatever it holds, so the span can be added up before the number is
known. Modbus/TCP's length excludes itself and this one includes itself, and the difference
is which set the edge points at rather than anything the engine has to be told.

about: ASHRAE 135 §20.1.4 — the answer to a Confirmed-Request, carrying whatever the service returns.
Two shapes, told apart by one bit of the first octet. Whole, the service's parameters are here
and readable. Segmented, what follows is a PIECE of them cut at whatever octet the window ran
out on — capture C3 stops halfway through an object identifier — so it is octets and nothing
more until the pieces are put back together, which happens across datagrams and not in one.

about: §15.5.1.2.4 wraps the value in parameter 3, and §20.2.1.3.2 makes that a pair of markers carrying NO length at all.

Which is the thing about BACnet that nothing else here does: what sits between them is bounded by finding the closing tag, not by a number. One deep, that is a tag whose length nibble is seven; nested, it is a count carried from one round to the next, and there is nowhere to keep one.
